findings.finding: Three sources bind, in TWO different custodies: the OCA model petition and order are Master Library assets, and the Statement of Inability is held in human_source_returns, a custody carried by no release and writing its paths relative to the repository root rather than a corpus root.
findings.consequence: Custody roots are resolved through the shared resolver, which follows what the corpus index declares rather than the shape of the path. Each source binds by exact SHA-256 against the index entry, the mounted bytes and this family's own pin, and any disagreement is a source stop that writes nothing.

findings.finding: The proposed order is the SAME BINARY, by SHA-256 (6a60f72a…), that the sibling § 411.0735 family binds, and the Statement of Inability is the same shared national record four Texas families enclose. Both were read first-hand from the pinned bytes here rather than copied from a sibling's entry.
findings.consequence: This family pins each by SHA-256 in its own SOURCES and records each digest in its own receipt, so its binding is legible without reading any other family's, and no other family's entry is changed.

findings.finding: This section exists for people who do NOT qualify for the AUTOMATIC order under Gov't Code § 411.072, whose order issues without any petition and whose only money is a $28 clerk fee. The registry carries "the person may qualify under Gov't Code 411.072 and that has not been ruled out" as a self-help stop condition.
findings.consequence: The packet says so before it says anything about filing this petition, in both the participant instructions and the filing guide, and directs the participant to pull their DPS criminal history record to see whether the offence is already sealed. Selling a paid petition to someone entitled to a free automatic order is the most expensive error available on this route, and staying silent about it would be how it happened.

findings.finding: The petition carries a three-way control for the waiting period, because § 411.0725 has THREE: the discharge and dismissal itself for a misdemeanour outside Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 and 46; the second anniversary for a misdemeanour inside them; and the fifth anniversary for a felony.
findings.consequence: The control is classified as an election determined by the participant's own offence rather than by this route, and is left unmarked. All three periods belong to § 411.0725, so marking one would not be stating which route the packet is built for — it would be swearing to a characterisation of the offence that only the participant's judgment can support. The guidance sets out all three and says the clock runs from the discharge and dismissal.

findings.finding: Paragraph 2 of the petition asks the participant to CHECK ALL THAT APPLY from five printed reasons why the § 411.072 automatic order is not available, and a sixth control records whether the list of prior convictions and deferred adjudications is attached.
findings.consequence: All six are classified as participant elections and left unmarked. Each is a sworn statement about the participant's own record — the Penal Code chapter of their offence, a finding filed in their case file, the grade of the offence, their other convictions, the date of their discharge — and the platform has seen none of those records. Every one is named in the participant instructions.

findings.finding: Gov't Code § 411.0745(b) requires a fee that generally applies to the filing of a CIVIL CASE. Read at source, the subsection sets the TYPE of fee and not an amount: county civil filing fee schedules govern. OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county. The registry carries the county figure as an UNRESOLVED QUESTION with impact release_blocker.
findings.consequence: The packet states exactly that — that the statute fixes the kind of fee and not the number, that OCA describes about $280 varying by county, and that the clerk of the court being filed in is the authority who answers it. No figure is published as though it were the fee, and the unresolved question is carried into the approval request rather than being resolved by this lane.

findings.finding: The committed record warns in terms that the $28 figure belongs ONLY to the no-petition route under Gov't Code § 411.072(c) and is not a filing fee. On this route that warning matters more than on any sibling, because § 411.072 is precisely the route this section catches the overflow from.
findings.consequence: The guidance names the $28 explicitly in order to tell the participant it is not theirs on this route. A participant who has just read about the automatic route will have met that number, and the packet is the only thing that could tell them it does not travel with them.

findings.finding: Section 411.0745(e) makes the COURT responsible for giving the State notice and an opportunity for a hearing, and the committed record states the filer should not be charged for it. OCA instructions separately direct the petitioner to show proof that the district attorney received a copy of the petition.
findings.consequence: The packet states that the court gives notice and that the participant serves nobody, and ships the proof-of-delivery page as a CONDITIONAL component whose own first paragraph tells the participant to ask the clerk whether that county wants it.

findings.finding: The petition's own printed blank (1) — the cause number at the top of page 1 — has NO AcroForm widget behind it. It is a printed underscore rule. Read first-hand from the pinned binary: 29 widgets over 6 pages, none of them on that line.
findings.consequence: There is nothing for this build to write into and nothing to declare in the field map, so the participant instructions name it explicitly as a line to write in by hand. A blank with no field behind it is invisible to every field-level counter, which is exactly why it is stated in prose instead.

findings.finding: Read first-hand from the pinned binary, NO field on this petition ships a value — unlike the § 411.0727 and § 411.0735 siblings, whose is/is-not dropdowns arrive carrying the form's own ink. Every widget on all three pinned sources was read for the annotation Hidden flag and none carries it: 0 of 29 widgets on the petition, 0 of 19 on the order, 0 of 141 on the Statement.
findings.consequence: The absence was measured here rather than inherited from a sibling's finding, and each pinned source is additionally flattened UNWRITTEN and compared, so a source-authored value could not be counted as a write by this build. No write in this family lands in a widget that would carry no ink.

findings.finding: The 'Type of Offense' control is a DROPDOWN offering misdemeanor or felony, and it is the fact that decides which of the three waiting periods applies.
findings.consequence: It is classified as a fact the participant supplies rather than as an election, because it is read off the judgment rather than chosen, and it is surfaced as a required-before-filing item so the participant is told to fill it. Classifying it as an election would have been the easier route through the counters and the less true description of the blank.

findings.finding: The registry carries two UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS for this route, both with impact release_blocker: the county-specific civil filing fee, and that the OCA models carry a February 2022 revision that has not been revised for the 2023 recodification of expunction into Chapter 55A.
findings.consequence: Both are read from the committed registry at build time and carried verbatim into this findings file and the approval request. Neither is this lane's to resolve, and a packet that did not carry them would read as though the record were settled.
